_: The Gradius comparison corpus. ONE file, read by BOTH sides: scen.py drives
the cartridge with it and porttrace.mjs drives the port with it, so the two
cannot drift apart the way two hand-kept copies of a script do.
Every script begins with the same 400-frame boot prefix, which is the one
PROBE.md already characterised: 200 idle frames, START, 190 more. Game mode
reaches 5 at frame 282, the ship's object becomes alive at 283, and the
stage-intro sub-state $1B holds the player frozen until frame ~310. Holds
therefore start at frame 400, clear of all three -- MEASURED at frame 400:
ALIGNMENT: the port does not model the title screen or the 28-frame stage
intro, so it cannot be booted cold and compared. The comparison SEEDS the
port from the cartridge's own RAM at frame `align` and free-runs from there.
That is the same arrangement NOTES-player.md 11 used for playermodel.py.
It is stated here because it bounds what the comparison proves: everything
BEFORE frame 400 is untested by this corpus, including src/main.js's
bootState().
POKE SYNTAX. `"poke": "0040=6"` holds a value for the whole compared
window; `"poke": "001F=1@+40"` writes it at ONE frame, align+40. Both are
applied at $80B5 -- after the sample -- on BOTH sides, so the first frame
they affect is the next one. Use the one-frame form for any value the
cartridge itself only ever holds for one frame; holding such a value is
testing invented state. See porttrace.mjs POKEABLE for what may be poked
and why each address is allowed.
_watch: Extra RAM added to probe.lua's state vector through its own --watch
mechanism, so the oracle is EXTENDED without being EDITED. Every address
here is one the port claims to model; nothing is watched for decoration.
The 48 ring bytes are the reason the Option comparison is worth anything:
comparing $0361/$0362 alone would pass for a port that trailed the ship by
the wrong number of ring entries on a straight-line hold.
ADDRESSES WATCHED AHEAD OF THE PORT: $19 $24 $4C (stage index, checkpoint,
the death countdown) are not modelled at all and carry a written reason in
porttrace.mjs UNMODELLED, so they are reported as SKIPPED, not as silent
nulls. They are here so that waves 4 and 5 are judged against cartridge
data recorded BEFORE the code that has to reproduce it was written.
WAVE 2 ADDED THE HUD'S STATE AND ITS INPUTS: $48 (the four-phase rotation,
$88A4 INC $48 -- real port state), and $20/$21 $42 $46 $07E0-$07EA, which
src/hud.js READS and nothing in the port yet WRITES. Watching a seeded
constant proves little on its own; it is here so that the frame waves 5-7
make it move is compared against data recorded now. src/state.js says the
same thing under SEEDED INPUTS, at the code.
WAVE 3 ADDED THE ENEMY POOL AND THE SPAWN ENGINE. Sixteen arrays x the ten
enemy slots 12-21 ($010C-$0115 status, $012C metasprite, $014C anim timer,
$016C anim frame, $018C palette OR, $030C type, $032C/$034C Y, $036C/$038C
X, $03AC carrier, $03BC/$03EC Y velocity, $042C X velocity / explosion
cursor, $040C the shot countdown / $04EC its reload, $046C handler state,
$048C sub-state, $04AC the second phase counter, $04CC unidentified but
cleared by $A527), plus the engine's own zero
WAVE 3'S TEST PASS ADDED THE THREE $A527 ARRAYS THE COMPARISON COULD NOT
SEE. src/enemies.js clearSlot() justifies its reading of the two Y-indexed
stores with 'the watch list compares addresses' -- and for $0460+j
($A52E) and $0480+22+j ($A52B) it did not: neither range was watched, so
dropping either store was green over all 18 scenarios and caught only by
tests/enemies.test.js. $044C-$0455 (the X sub-pixel velocity $B154 adds)
was the one of the twenty-one X-indexed arrays that was missing too.
Watched now: $044C-$0455, $0460-$0469, $0496-$049F. They are constant zero
across this corpus -- that is the POINT: the port must keep them zero, and
wave 6's $BE93 is the first code that will make them move.
$6A:$6B is the one to look at hardest. It is a REAL CPU POINTER into the
ROM's wave lists, and comparing it is what makes the wave-record walk
checkable rather than merely plausible: 00-recon-enemies.md 1 recorded it
stepping $A846 -> $A848 -> ... -> $A858 as each of chunk 0's ten records
fired, and $A85B after the chunk switch at scroll $0200. A port that
abstracted the wave list into an array index could not be held to that.
_knownFail: docs/knowledge/01: annotate known-unfixable divergence rather than deleting
the scenario, and make an unexpected PASS fail the run so nobody forgets to
remove the annotation. Each entry names the fields, the mechanism, and the
measurement that established it. Nothing is listed here that has not been
traced to a specific instruction on the cartridge.
THE LIST IS EMPTY, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF WAVE 2. It held exactly one
entry for the port's whole life -- `terrain-streams-at-double-rate`, over
w_000E w_0054 w_0055 w_0057 w_0058 -- and it was removed in the SAME commit
that ported $8898 (src/hud.js), because compare.mjs FAILS on a knownFail
that no longer diverges. Both measured causes are closed:
A ($8641, wave 1) $80B0 appends ONE $00 -- the drainer's mode-0 stop byte
-- on every non-lag frame. Without it w_000E read one low on frame 401,
the FIRST compared frame.
B ($8898, wave 2) the HUD tick shares the terrain streamer's $0E gate and
runs seven bytes above it ($9AC7 vs $9ACE), producing 8/14/39 bytes on
ODD $02 frames. Measured: entered 390, past both gates 195, even 0 and
odd 195; build histogram {0:196, 1:195} on the cartridge against
{0:1, 1:390} on the port; and starving the cartridge's own gate turned
it INTO the port while both sides still emitted the same 140 blocks.
So the divergence was a phase error in $54/$55/$57/$58/$0E, never a content
error in VRAM. Those five fields are TIER 1 again. If one of them starts
diverging that is a REGRESSION in src/hud.js or src/terrain.js -- do not
re-annotate it here without a fresh measurement of its own.

scenarios.name: enemy-waves
scenarios.why:
THE ENEMY SCENARIO. 1465 compared frames -- long enough for all ten of stage 1's chunk-0 wave records (fired at game frames 378 before the align, then 506, 634, 762, 890, 954, 1018, 1082, 1146, 1210), the $FF terminator, the CHUNK SWITCH at scroll $0200 (frame 1339, cursor $A858 -> $A85B), and chunk 1's first four records. Three enemy types are dispatched in the window: $05/$85 the fan ($B0AF, 4840 dispatches), $08/$88 the wavy one ($B26C, 3954) and $04/$84 the arc ($B205, 570, first at frame 1722). It also covers one natural ALLOCATION FAILURE at frame 1152, which is the behaviour that drops a member and collapses a squadron's spacing.

WHY RD, AND WHY IT IS THE ONLY CHOICE. Without weapons the ship cannot kill anything, and every enemy in stage 1's opening homes on the player's Y, so it dies -- MEASURED, first death frame per 1460-frame hold: idle 1051, R 493, RU 445, U 1076, L ~1180. compare.mjs truncates at the death, and a death also RESETS THE CAMERA at the respawn (measured: after the L-run's death the spawn engine re-fired chunk 0's first record at scroll $0020, frame 1299), so the chunk switch never happens. RD parks the ship in the bottom-right corner at (240,192), where the fan's return leg and the wavy one's approach both miss: it survives to frame 1865 and dies at 1866, which is where this scenario stops. Nothing else in the corpus reaches past frame 640.

The cartridge's one lag frame in this run is at game frame 283, i.e. before the align -- so romLagInWindow is 0 and the lag comparison still has teeth via long-idle.

scenarios.name: long-idle
scenarios.why: The same zero-load baseline, run for 600 frames instead of 240. Added for one reason and it is stated: the 240-frame scenarios contain three natural lag frames and every one of them falls AFTER its scenario's death truncation, so `lagged` was a compared field that could not fail on any live window. A longer live run is the only way to make the cartridge's own timing part of the comparison rather than a footnote.

scenarios.name: s0-handover
scenarios.why: THE SPRITE-0 HANDOVER, injected for exactly ONE frame (game 440). Added because two agents independently deleted `state.zp1E !== 0` and `state.zp1F !== 0` from the split gate in src/nmi.js and got byte-identical output from all 16 other scenarios: $1E = 1 and $1F = 2 on every one of their 3341 compared frames, so both terms of $9A8C/$9A90 were unfalsifiable -- docs/knowledge/03's third shape. $9C38 (`A9 01 85 1F`) is the cartridge writing this value itself, during the stage intro, which is before align 400 and inside a sub-state the port does not model; hence the injection. It is ONE frame because $8B1A-$8B2B promotes 1 to 2 on the next build, so a held 1 is a state the cartridge is never in. What the frame after the poke must show, on BOTH sides: $1F 1 -> 2, $1E still 0, the LIVE sprite-0 record in OAM, NO split, and the camera $3D/$3E/$3F held for that one frame because $9A8E branches past $9AA0 as well as past the split.
scenarios._: Idle rather than moving on purpose: the ONLY difference between this scenario and `idle` is the one poked frame, so any divergence is that frame's or its consequences and cannot be confused with a player-input effect.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.why: Nothing held. The zero-load baseline NOTES-lag.md experiment 1 asks for, and the one scenario in which the position ring must NOT advance ($A082: AND #$0F, no direction -> the whole Option chain freezes). A port that advanced the ring every frame passes every moving scenario and fails only this one.

scenarios.name: right-wall
scenarios.why: 80 -> 240 at 1 px/frame takes 160 frames, then 80 more frames sitting on the $A028 CMP #$F0 clamp. The tail is the point: there is NO pre-check on X, so at the wall the integer is re-clamped every frame while $0380 keeps accumulating.

scenarios.name: left-wall
scenarios.why: 80 -> 16 in 64 frames, then 176 frames on the $A03A CMP #$10 clamp. Long tail because the X sub-pixel byte $0380 keeps moving there and a port that freezes it drifts only slowly.

scenarios.name: up-wall
scenarios.why: 96 -> 16 in 80 frames, then 160 on the ceiling. UP's pre-check is $A06E BCC, i.e. it blocks only BELOW $10 -- so UP still RUNS at Y == $10 and still moves $0340. The asymmetry with DOWN is only visible here.

scenarios.name: down-wall
scenarios.why: 96 -> 192 in 96 frames, then 144 on the floor. DOWN's pre-check is $A054 BCS, which blocks AT $C0: at the floor DOWN writes nothing at all -- not the integer, not $0340, not the tilt -- and falls through into the UP test.

scenarios.name: diag-rd-lu
scenarios.why: Two of the four diagonals. There is no diagonal arm in $9FFC: X is done, then Y is done, with the SAME $99:$98 step, so a diagonal covers step*sqrt(2). A port that normalised diagonal speed diverges here and nowhere else.

scenarios.name: diag-ru-ld
scenarios.why: The other two diagonals, so all four are covered and the tilt latch is driven by both nose-up and nose-down inside one run.

scenarios.name: corner-br
scenarios.why: Into the bottom-right corner and then let go. Both clamps at once, and the 40 idle frames at the end check that the ring stops advancing while the ship is parked somewhere other than its start position.

scenarios.name: corner-tl
scenarios.why: Into the top-left corner, the other pair of clamps, with the UP-at-the-ceiling asymmetry active for 120 of the 200 frames.

scenarios.name: lr-both
scenarios.why: $A031 is a FALL-THROUGH target, not an else. LEFT+RIGHT runs BOTH arms: add, clamp, subtract, clamp. Away from a wall the net displacement is zero -- but the ring still advances, because $A082 tests AND #$0F and does not care that the ship did not move.

scenarios.name: ud-both
scenarios.why: UP+DOWN. DOWN is tested first so it normally wins, but the 100 DOWN frames park the ship on the floor first, where DOWN's pre-check declines and UP is honoured instead. A port that gave DOWN unconditional priority is green for the first 100 frames and red after.

scenarios.name: speed6-right
scenarios.why: SPEED level 6, i.e. step = min(6+2,16)*128 = $0400 = 4.0 px/frame. ADDED BECAUSE THE BUTTON-ONLY CORPUS WAS BLIND: $40 reads 0 on every frame the cartridge produces from a script, so `step` is exactly $0100, the low byte is zero, and both sub-pixel accumulators stay 0 forever. A mutation that deleted the fraction add from $A285 altogether left the comparison GREEN over 2,860 frames. $40 = 6 is a level the cartridge itself reaches ($89A1 INC $40) and it makes $0380 move on every frame.

scenarios.name: speed3-diag
scenarios.why: SPEED level 3: step = 5*128 = $0280, so the fraction byte is $80 and CARRIES every second frame. That is the case that separates a real 16-bit accumulator from an integer one -- an integer port is right on half the frames, which is exactly how this class of bug survives. Diagonal, so both $0340 and $0380 carry independently.

scenarios.name: opt2-wiggle
scenarios.why: TWO OPTIONS. $45 is 0 in every button-only scenario, so $A0C8's loop (LDX $45 / DEX / BMI) never executes a single iteration and $0121/$0122/$0141/$0142 are 0 on every compared frame -- the Options track the player but are never DRAWN. With $45 = 2 the loop runs, the Options get metasprite ids 4 and 5 alternating every 8 frames, and they enter the display list.

scenarios.name: wiggle
scenarios.why: Taps and gaps. The tilt latch only samples $9B every 8 frames ($A0BA CMP #$08), so short holds and the gaps between them are the only thing that exercises which frame the latch lands on; and the ring's stop/start is what makes the Option lag a lag in RING ENTRIES rather than in frames.
